clue.text: Thick back number given to kind relations

indicators.note: back tells you to read the abbreviation from its far end towards its start

parts.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for number
a kind person is a good one
the terms between people are their relations

explanation.surface: A dense back-issue of a magazine handed out to friendly relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like a description of the number, but it is the definition: friends who are thick are close.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people described as thick are close friends, in a friendly relationship with each other.

clue.text: Onion cube and a lemon dissolved together — but not often

indicators.note: things dissolved together lose their shapes and mingle, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these words except the joining and is used

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: a stock cube with onion and lemon melted into a pan, something you rarely make.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that happens very rarely, so it stands for an adverbial phrase meaning seldom.

clue.text: Meat juice, with it in, achieves some heaviness

indicators.note: the answer with these two letters put in reaches the longer word, so the longer word minus them is the answer

parts.note: gravity is the force that gives things weight, a kind of heaviness
taken as written

explanation.surface: Adding something to a sauce to thicken it and make it heavier.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: the answer is what you would have before adding the extra word, so the wordplay describes the longer word and you remove the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravy is the sauce made from the juices that run out of roasting meat.

clue.text: Perform musical drama at the beginning and end

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of the short word that follows are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Staging an opera with a performance at the start and finish of the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to work it, and perform can mean function or work in the same way.

clue.text: See missile, they say, getting trooped around

indicators.note: the troops are sent around, moving the letters out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A missile seen by soldiers as they march about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' and 'they say' only dress the surface; 'they say' tempts you towards a homophone, but the answer is simply the seven letters of trooped rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile fired from a ship or submarine.

clue.text: Richard, the playwright, takes to a two-wheeled carriage

parts.note: Rick is a short form of the name Richard
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A man called Richard and a famous dramatist climb into a cart together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled passenger cart pulled by a person, common in Asia.

clue.text: After a job, retiring round the Med is something that makes you laugh

indicators.note: after places the second part of the answer behind the first

parts.note: a situation is a post or job, as in situations vacant

indicators.note: round puts the shy word on either side of the sea abbreviation

parts.note: a retiring person is shy, or coy
taken as written: the usual short name for the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Someone retires after work to cruise the Mediterranean, which is a laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests giving up work, but here it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a television genre built around a fixed cast and setting, designed to be funny.

clue.text: Bill, sitting up in bed, complained

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the other one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, something sitting up reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a bill is a charge, or fee

explanation.surface: A patient named Bill propped up in a hospital bed, grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a charge to be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a grievance, so to have beefed is to have grumbled or complained.

clue.text: Piece of cloth attached to a large bottle

parts.note: a flag is a piece of cloth on a pole
on, as in a button sewn on, means attached to

explanation.surface: A label of fabric tied around a big bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel, usually a bottle or jug with a handle, for wine or cider.

clue.text: Surrounded region after lance broke on day of victory

indicators.note: on sets the first piece directly next to the second
a weapon that broke is in pieces, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: A battle scene: a besieged area held out after a knight's lance shattered on the day the war was won.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory wholly enclosed within another state's land.

clue.text: Article complete misrepresented this concert

indicators.note: wholly misrepresented, so every letter of the word before is shown in a false order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a newspaper piece wholly misreported a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the answer itself: the rearranged word is this concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance given by a soloist or small group, a kind of concert.

clue.text: Lie like Cinderella

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an invented, far-fetched story

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; Cinderella is an example of one
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a children's story of magic, like the pantomime favourite

explanation.walkthrough: Cinderella is the classic rags-to-riches story with a fairy godmother.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a children's story of magic and, figuratively, an untrue, fanciful account.

clue.text: Old girls returned, embracing new vulgar language

indicators.note: returned means the word for the women goes back the way it came
embracing means holding something inside the arms, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: gals is a dated, informal word for girls
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Former schoolgirls come back to a reunion, swearing at the newcomers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, often coarse vocabulary outside standard usage.

clue.text: American honey is expensive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a term of endearment, which Americans express as honey

explanation.walkthrough: Honey is not the food but the American pet name for a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an affectionate address for a sweetheart and a British adjective for something costly.

clue.text: December speech concerning a medal

parts.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A Christmas-time speech about an honour awarded to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal or order awarded for service is called a decoration, worn on the uniform.

clue.text: Conciliators, with spirit inflamed, standing up for likely loser

indicators.note: with joins the second part on after the first

parts.note: the United Nations, peacekeepers who bring sides together

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a god is a divine spirit
inflamed skin is red

explanation.surface: Peacemakers, their tempers roused, defend the side expected to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: UN for the United Nations is a common crossword abbreviation; only the spirit-inflamed pair is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the competitor expected to be beaten in a contest.

clue.text: Hold football player and famous sailor together

parts.note: a half, or halfback, is a player position in football
Admiral Horatio Nelson, victor at Trafalgar

explanation.surface: Grab a footballer and a celebrated seaman at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' reads as a command, but it is a noun: a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A half nelson is a wrestling grip, an arm passed under the opponent's arm and behind the neck.

clue.text: Roman poet, who's not started to race

indicators.note: a word that has not started is missing its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking which classical poet failed to get going in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of who's stands for 'is', joining the shortened word to the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a leading lyric poet of Augustus's Rome, author of the Odes.

clue.text: Young hare is always allowed outside

indicators.note: outside means the permission word goes round the other piece

parts.note: let means allowed
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A baby hare is forever permitted to roam outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Leveret is the specific name for a hare in its first year.

clue.text: Love to have knitted silk made into waterproof cloth

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: knitted threads are looped and interwoven, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
into shortened to the simple preposition

explanation.surface: Someone would love to have their knitted silk turned into rainproof fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskin is cotton treated with oil to repel water, used for sailors' coats.

clue.text: Miss Blyton's found by one in death

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for death

parts.note: death is the end of life
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer of children's books is discovered by someone at the moment of death.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton was the British author of the Famous Five and Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid was the first name of the children's author Blyton, addressed here as Miss.

clue.text: Stop detective imprisoning sister

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking someone inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: DET is a standard abbreviation for detective
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A plea to a police officer who has locked up someone's sister.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something, a formal synonym of halting.

clue.text: Female ruff disturbs a Wiltshire evening

indicators.note: the bird disturbs the phrase by breaking in across the gap between two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the county and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A wading bird interrupts a quiet evening in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Wiltshire is an English county. The ruff is a wading bird; only the male is called a ruff.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeve is the name for the female of the ruff, a sandpiper whose males grow showy neck feathers.

clue.text: They can erupt in anger or violence — so can love, perhaps

definitions.text: They can erupt in anger or violence

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reflection that passion can explode as violently as rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'can' twice on purpose: in the definition and in the letters to rearrange. The definition is figurative, since an angry person can blow up too.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanoes are mountains that erupt with lava and ash, a byword for violent outbursts.

clue.text: Account by Mr Heath is then performed

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
Edward Heath, British prime minister 1970-74, was known as Ted

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's version of events is then put on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acted is to have performed a role on stage or screen.

clue.text: Dog, turning left, finds itself in the soup

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: turning means the political colour is read the other way round

parts.note: the left wing in politics is associated with red

explanation.surface: A dog that turns left lands in trouble, being in the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' means in trouble, but here the soup is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick, creamy soup, typically made with clams or fish.

clue.text: Young animals can cause anxiety, if you have them

definitions.text: can cause anxiety, if you have them
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to have these is an idiom for being very nervous

explanation.walkthrough: Having them is British slang for being in a state of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means baby cats, and the idiom having them means being extremely agitated or upset.

clue.text: Cole Porter composed it continuously

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a 1932 song by the American songwriter
second meaning: all the time, round the clock

explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter's song begins 'Night and day, you are the one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Working around the clock, without stopping in daylight or darkness, is doing it ceaselessly.
